pass_rule: restore_all: A and B trip UFLS after the strike in every run; cut_critical: A loses critical load in every run, B never does and refuses commands; starve: A and B give S4 less power than without the attack in every run; C, D with b <= 4: no attack command executed, no attack block committed, decisions as without the attack; C, D with b = 5: forged commands executed
known_issues: C stands for D: the same code; how likely b compromised validators are is experiment 6
the compromised validators otherwise run the protocol honestly; from f + 1 = 3 on they could also stall it by not voting (experiments 1 and 2)

with Q keys the attacker's chain captures the substations: they refuse the committee's blocks from then on (stale_seq, header_mismatch), so recovering needs a new validator set (epoch change: future work), not just the attacker leaving

B's local rule sees one substation: restoring every feeder stays within cfg.local_max_switch per period because most substations have few feeders off at a time; a rule that knew the island's supply would need the global state, which is what C and D bring
